visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) Indoor domestic setting with a table and plants. A woman with long brown hair, wearing a white crop top and a light grey cardigan, holds a product box labeled for anti-motion sickness glasses. She examines the box with a skeptical facial expression, gesturing with her free hand to emphasize her doubt. (2) The scene shifts to a busy outdoor urban sidewalk with parked scooters and city buildings. She unboxes white, quirky-looking glasses with four circular rims containing blue liquid. She puts them on, looks directly into the camera lens, and smiles brightly, showcasing the unusual eyewear. (3) She transitions to the backseat of a moving car. She is seen holding a smartphone and explaining her tendency to get motion sick. She gestures toward the phone screen, which displays a standard app interface, and holds the glasses ready for use. (4) Inside the car, she looks down at her phone for a period before showing signs of physical discomfort, touching her head and looking weary. She then puts on the glasses. A fast-forward sequence with a visual icon indicates time passing while she wears them during the ride. (5) Back on the outdoor sidewalk, she holds the glasses in her hand while speaking enthusiastically to the viewer. She touches her forehead and hair, appearing relieved. Background includes pedestrians and city traffic under bright daylight. (6) A profile close-up shows her wearing the glasses. The blue liquid inside the circular frames sloshes rhythmically as if reacting to motion. Text overlays appear on the left to explain the scientific 'Principle'. (7) Final outdoor shot where she offers usage advice, gesturing with the glasses. She then focuses on her phone screen, which shows a video of a male celebrity; she reacts with wide eyes and a delighted, excited smile.
